transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. What brings you in to see me today?
Once I start eating late at night after my shift, I feel like I can’t stop or control how much I’m eating. It's really started to worry me, so I figured it was time to come in and talk to someone.
Can you describe a typical episode where you feel like you've lost control over your eating, and how often do these episodes occur?

I'll get home after midnight and plow through a couple of drive-thru bags, then go to the kitchen for leftover casserole or half a loaf of bread, just shoveling it in on autopilot. It feels like a switch flips and I can't stop myself, and this has been happening several times a week for the last three or four months.
Do you also experience a lack of control or excessive engagement in other behaviors, such as excessive spending, substance use, or hypersexual behavior, around the same time as these eating episodes?
No, I don't have any of those other issues like excessive spending or substance use. This loss of control is strictly focused on my late-night eating when I get home from work.
Do you often feel guilty or ashamed after these late-night eating episodes, or do you tend to justify them as a way to cope with your work schedule or other stressors?

It definitely started as a way to decompress from the stress and messed-up routine of my new night-shift supervisor job, but now it just leads to intense guilt. I'll sit there alone staring at the empty containers feeling gross, beating myself up that a grown man and a supervisor can't control himself around food.
Can you tell me if during these episodes, you're eating because you're physically hungry or because you feel an overwhelming urge to eat, regardless of whether you're hungry or full?

I might start out feeling hungry and wired after a long night shift, but it quickly turns into an overwhelming urge where I'm just eating on autopilot. Even when I'm completely full and my stomach is painfully tight, I keep shoving food in because I feel totally unable to stop myself.
During these episodes of eating on autopilot, do you ever experience any emotional numbing or a sense of being detached from yourself, as if you're watching yourself eat without being able to stop?

I wouldn't say I feel emotionally numb or like I'm watching myself from outside my body. It's more of a physical loss of control, where my hands just keep grabbing food on autopilot and I can't seem to make them stop. I'm fully there and aware, I just feel like I'm not the one calling the shots.
Can you estimate how many calories you typically consume during one of these late-night eating episodes, and does this amount significantly exceed what you would normally eat in a single sitting?

I don't track calories, so I'm not sure of the exact number, but it is definitely a massive amount that way exceeds a normal sitting. I'll polish off a couple of drive-thru bags, leftover casserole, half a loaf of bread, and pantry snacks all at once. It's honestly enough food to feed a family of four, and it's all just me.
Do you typically experience significant weight gain or other physical health consequences as a result of these frequent late-night eating episodes?

Yes, I've had some rapid weight gain that was noticeable enough for my wife and pastor to comment on. Physically, I eat until my stomach is so tight and stretched that it hurts to bend over to take off my work boots, and I end up feeling really sluggish and stuffed the next day.
Do you experience any episodes of eating in response to emotional states, such as anxiety or sadness, outside of the late-night post-work context?
No, I haven't really noticed myself eating like this outside of that late-night, post-work timeframe. It seems almost entirely tied to coming home feeling stressed and wired after my night shift.
